confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from aggregated Numbeo-based figures (dated June 2026, as cited by Expatica) in three web searches, converted at an assumed GBP/USD rate of about 1.32. The figures are approximately: cappuccino £4.11, inexpensive meal £20, mid-range meal for two £81, and 0.5 L draught beer £7.08. Pub pint guides gave £6-7.50, so beer is set slightly below the Numbeo figure. Cocktail and wine by the glass are less certain. The only cocktail figure found was an old 2020 guide price of about £11. Wine-by-the-glass was a £7-12 guide range. Both are therefore set from their usual relationship to London beer prices and the guide ranges. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates, not based on any searches or live listings. They assume July peak-season demand and vary a lot by location.
comparable_city_reasoning: London is treated as its own market, one of Europe's most expensive cities. Its prices are close to those of other top-tier Western European capitals such as Paris and Dublin, but it has a higher accommodation premium in peak summer.
